newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Petrobras, YPF mull 1,500 joint service stations.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras, YPF mull 1,500 joint service stations.

text.p: Brazil's state-owned Petrobras and Argentina's YPF SA are studying opening 1,500 service stations as part of a $750 million joint venture, company officials said Wednesday.

The service stations -- which would be installed in greater Buenos Aires and in southern Brazil -- are one of the top projects of a new holding company created by the two firms, Petrobras Argentina SA Vice President Jose Fernando de Freitas said.

"For these projects which are more or less identified, like service stations in the two countries, lubricants, grease, and liquid petroleum gas, we are estimating a total joint investment of $750 million over five years," he told Reuters.

De Freitas was speaking after the ceremonial signing in Buenos Aires of the agreement to create the new holding by the the presidents of the two firms -- each the largest oil company in their respective countries.
About 15 percent of the new service stations, which would display both the YPF and Petrobras logos, would be owned by the holding, while the rest would be franchises, he said.

The new company's service stations could in some cases compete with existing YPF or Petrobras stations, De Freitas said, but should be well placed to take advantage of new opportunities in expanding markets.

"There are going to be some cases where YPF in Argentina and Petrobras in Brazil could lose a bit of market share to this new company, but if that happens you have to take into account that those service stations affected are not very profitable or not very competitive," de Freitas said. "The thing is that we are installing a new company that will seek a new market niche for better growth."
He stressed that separate YPF and Petrobras service stations will continue to run and expand their own separate service stations.

The Petrobras-YPF venture, which will serve as a holding company, will act in the purchase and resale of liquid and gas fuels, transportation, storage and refining of petroleum and petrochemical products.
Petrobras and YPF will each hold 50 percent of the new company which will also be involved in the import and export of petroleum products.
The presidents of Petrobras and YPF also signed an agreement creating the so-called Mega Project, 38 percent owned by YPF, 34 percent by Petrobras and 28 percent by Dow Chemical.

The $650 million project seeks to develop natural gas fields in Argentina's Neugina Basin with the construction of a liquid gas separation plant, a 375-mile (600-km) gas pipeline and a fractionating unit in the city of Bahia Blanca.
Once operating within three years, the project will produce about 516,000 tonnes a year of ethane to be sold to Argentina's Petroquimica Bahia Blanca.
Approximately 615,000 tonnes of liquified petroleum gas and 188,000 tonnes of primary gasoline will be exported each year to Brazil.
